capital.heading: Water, heat and light, and a nation of readers.

register.name: Landsvirkjun green bonds, US private placement, 2026
register.detail: Landsvirkjun · issued 28 May 2026 · two tranches, six and eight years · fixed 5.33%, 115 basis points over US Treasuries; floating SOFR plus 169 basis points · upsized from US$180M · demand above four times the amount offered
register.note: Proceeds for new power projects, including the Vaðalda Wind Farm, Iceland’s first wind farm: 28 turbines, 120 MW
register.text: Green bonds of Landsvirkjun, the National Power Company of Iceland, placed in the US private placement market under its Green Finance Framework. The proceeds finance new power projects, including the Vaðalda Wind Farm, planned to be in full operation before the end of 2027. It serves the energy standard, keeping new supply renewable.

register.name: Landsvirkjun green bonds, US private placement, 2025
register.detail: Landsvirkjun · issued 15 May 2025 · three tranches, six and eight years · fixed 5.17% and 5.37%, 115 to 125 basis points over US Treasuries; floating SOFR plus 144 basis points · upsized from US$125M · covenant-free
register.note: Proceeds for the Vaðalda Wind Farm and the Hvammur Hydropower Station
register.text: Green bonds of Landsvirkjun, the National Power Company of Iceland, placed in the US private placement market under its Green Finance Framework, which sends proceeds only to assets or projects with positive environmental and climate impacts. They finance the Vaðalda Wind Farm and the Hvammur Hydropower Station, the eighth plant in the Þjórsá and Tungnaá region. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: City of Reykjavík green bonds (RVKG 48 1 and RVKNG 40 1)
register.detail: City of Reykjavík · RVKG 48 1, first issued 17 December 2018, due 21 October 2048, ISK 14.545bn · RVKNG 40 1, first issued 15 December 2020, due 21 August 2040, ISK 9.13bn · issued totals at 31 December 2025 · no new issue in 2025
register.note: Green Bond Impact Report 2025, 13 May 2026: eligible projects of ISK 24,709.9M in total
register.text: Two green bond series of the City of Reykjavík, issued under its Green Bond Framework, with ISK 23.675 billion issued at the end of 2025. The eligible projects include Dalskóli, a BREEAM-certified preschool, primary school and after-school programme (ISK 5,562 million), the Miðborg preschool, LED street lighting and cycling and walking paths. Dalskóli serves the education standard, the one furthest from reach.

register.name: Hellisheiði geothermal plant, heat production (Reykjavík Energy)
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · loan dated 13 April 2026 · ISK 4,625M, EUR 32M · 10 years · EUR 32.1M disbursed · total cost ISK 6,338M, investments of 2025–2027
register.note: 75,000 MWh a year of additional renewable heat during peak demand
register.text: An NIB loan to Orkuveita Reykjavíkur (Reykjavík Energy) to co-finance more thermal production at the Hellisheiði geothermal power plant, a new production well and a maintenance and storage facility. Peak hot-water demand grows by 120 litres per second each year, and the investments strengthen security of supply, especially at peak demand. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Municipal projects (Municipality Credit Iceland)
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · loan dated 16 December 2025 · ISK 3,500M, EUR 23.8M · 7 years · on-lent to projects aligned with NIB’s mandate
register.note: MCI has lent to schools, sport facilities, district heating, social housing and waste collection
register.text: An NIB loan to Lánasjóður sveitarfélaga (Municipality Credit Iceland), which borrows and lends on favourable terms to Icelandic municipalities, to finance municipal projects. Its lending includes schools, district heating and social housing, which serve the education, energy and shelter standards.

register.name: National grid upgrades (Landsnet)
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · loan dated 12 September 2025 · USD 35M, EUR 29.5M · 15 years · EUR 29.8M disbursed · financed from NIB Environmental Bond proceeds
register.note: Underground cables Akureyri–Dalvík (42 km) and Hella–Rimakot (36 km), and two submarine cables to the Westman Islands
register.text: An NIB loan to Landsnet, Iceland’s transmission system operator, for three grid projects: underground cables between Akureyri and Dalvík and between Hella and Rimakot, and two new submarine cables reinforcing the link to the Westman Islands. They improve security of supply, reduce transmission losses and support growing demand. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Hot water distribution and utility systems (Reykjavík Energy)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved, news of 27 September 2024 · Public Sector Financing Facility loan
register.note: Water and heating networks for a growing capital area, more resilient to crises
register.text: A CEB loan to Reykjavík Energy that will finance climate mitigation through the renewal and expansion of its hot water distribution systems, with upgrades to its water and heating networks for the city’s growing population and greater resilience to crises. It serves the energy and water standards.

register.name: Volcanic crisis on the Reykjanes peninsula, emergency and relief
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved, news of 7 June 2024 · Public Sector Financing Facility · borrower the Government of Iceland · an initial 70% expected to be disbursed early
register.note: Includes a voluntary government purchase of homes from residents of Grindavík, evacuated on 10 November 2023
register.text: A CEB loan to the Government of Iceland for its emergency and relief measures in the volcanic crisis on the Reykjanes peninsula: evacuation and emergency services, immediate help for the residents of Grindavík, a voluntary programme to buy the homes of residents who own property in the affected area, and early recovery. It serves the shelter standard for the families of an evacuated town.

register.name: Pre-school and compulsory school buildings (City of Reykjavík)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · signed 6 June 2024, ahead of the CEB’s 57th Joint Meeting, held in Iceland · part of a €223M investment programme for 2023–2028
register.note: Almost 22,500 children, including migrant and Ukrainian refugee children and children displaced from Grindavík
register.text: A CEB loan to the City of Reykjavík for major maintenance to upgrade its pre-school and compulsory school buildings, improving their quality, safety and health standards and creating modern learning spaces. The investments benefit almost 22,500 children. It serves the education standard, the one furthest from reach in Iceland.

register.name: Municipal financing in Iceland 4 (Municipality Credit Iceland)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 18 November 2021 · programme loan · status In progress on the CEB page · at least 50% expected for green investments
register.note: Urban and rural public infrastructure, public services and energy efficiency in municipalities across Iceland
register.text: A CEB programme loan to Municipality Credit Iceland, the lender to Icelandic municipalities and municipal companies, to co-finance investments that revitalise and modernise urban and rural public infrastructure, improve public services and save energy. It serves the living conditions of residents of the participating municipalities, and the energy standard through energy efficiency.

register.name: Nursing home and healthcare facilities in Reykjavík (Reitir)
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · loan dated 14 April 2026 · ISK 4,375M, about EUR 29M · 10 years · conversion of two former office buildings
register.note: A nursing home for 87 residents, scheduled to open in the first half of 2027, and new operating rooms, a pharmacy and radiology
register.text: An NIB loan to Reitir, an Icelandic real estate company, to co-finance the conversion of two former office buildings in Reykjavík: one into a nursing home of about 6,500 square metres for 87 residents, the other into healthcare facilities with operating rooms, a pharmacy and radiology, to be run by the private clinic Klíníkin. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Arion Bank Blue Economy Loan
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20250375 · approved 16 December 2025 · signed 19 December 2025 · announced 10 February 2026 · tranches of €80M for Iceland and €10M each for Greenland and the Faroe Islands
register.note: For small and medium-sized companies in sustainable fishing, seafood processing and fish and algae farming, with projects of 2026–2029
register.text: An EIB intermediated framework loan to Arion Bank, one of Iceland’s three largest banks, under an EIB instrument for sustainable investment in EFTA countries, for lending on to small and medium-sized marine businesses. All fisheries and aquaculture projects must be certified under internationally recognised schemes, such as the Marine Stewardship Council or the Aquaculture Stewardship Council. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2016
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17.5% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: Bjarg Housing Foundation (Bjarg íbúðafélag)
items.text: An independent non-profit housing foundation, established in December 2016 by the Icelandic Confederation of Labour (ASÍ) and BSRB, that builds and lets stable, long-term rental homes for low-income individuals and families; by October 2024 it had built and delivered more than a thousand homes to tenants, with around 500 more in preparation, design or construction.

items.name: Samhjálp
items.text: A non-profit that has worked for more than five decades with people living in poverty and social isolation; its soup kitchen Kaffistofan is open every day of the year and serves around 100,000 meals a year, up to 250 a day, and it runs the Hlaðgerðarkot rehabilitation home for 30 people and supported homes in Reykjavík and Kópavogur.

items.name: Hrafnista
items.text: A group of nursing homes that opened a new 80-place nursing home at Nesvellir in Reykjanesbær on 15 January 2026, built under the oversight of Sjómannadagsráð, which brings seven decades of experience in running nursing homes, after 64 new nursing places at Hrafnista Boðaþing in Kópavogur in September 2025.

items.name: Sólheimar
items.text: An eco-village founded in 1930 on the vision of a society where people with and without special needs live and work together; it grows vegetables in organic greenhouses, runs woodworking, ceramics and candle-making workshops and sells organic vegetables and products crafted by residents in its café and shop, with a guesthouse for visitors.

items.name: Brynja leigufélag
items.text: A rental housing company that builds and buys homes for disabled people and spreads them across ordinary neighbourhoods, mainly by buying single apartments in apartment blocks, and has built serviced houses in Reykjavík, Hafnarfjörður, Reykjanesbær and Egilsstaðir; in 2024 it was working with the housing cooperative Búseti to build at least 27 more apartments.

items.name: Hringsjá
items.text: An education and vocational rehabilitation centre in Reykjavík (Hringsjá náms- og starfsendurhæfing) that the Ministry of Education and Children recognised on 23 September 2024 as a provider of adult education for three years, to 23 September 2027.
